Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring voluntary measures to be included in critical area development to the extent possible.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to voluntary measures to protect critical areas;adding a new section to chapter 36.70A RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that there is abroadly held ethic among the citizens of the state that includesappreciation of nature and environmental values, and that citizens arewilling to voluntarily undertake activities to protect and enhanceenvironmental values at their homes and gardens, on land on which theylive or work, and in their communities. The legislature finds thatvoluntary activities can be invaluable toward achieving the overallgoal of protecting and enhancing the environment and that suchactivities should be given recognition as highly valued endeavors. The legislature finds that there are successful programs that canbe used as models, such as the "Shore Stewards Guide for ShorelineLiving" jointly prepared by university extension faculty and localgovernments, that provide information on a broad array of actions thatcitizens can undertake that fits their unique conditions and interests.The legislature finds that better enabling citizens to undertakevoluntary activities can in many circumstances be advantageous. p. 1 SSB 5301 The purpose of this act is to encourage counties and cities toexpand the availability and use of education, incentives, and otherprograms to help implement the comprehensive plans and developmentregulations required by chapter 36.70A RCW and to encourage andincrease the information and resources available to the public and tofoster voluntary activities by citizens to improve their environment.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 36.70A RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: To aid in carrying out the comprehensive plans and developmentregulations required by this chapter, counties and cities shall employvoluntary measures, incentives, and educational programs, to thegreatest extent possible, where they can be effective.
